episodes.title: Brain Fog, Part 1 - Is Your Brain in a Fog?

description.full:
What does brain fog actually feel like, and what may be happening beneath slow thinking, low mental energy, poor focus, memory slips, or trouble finding words?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains brain fog as a sign worth investigating rather than something to dismiss as a normal part of age or stress.

Topics include:

  • How brain fog can affect thinking speed, focus, memory, language, and mental stamina
  • Brain inflammation, microglia, neurotransmitters, and oxygen delivery
  • Potential contributors including concussion, autoimmunity, blood-sugar swings, hormones, mold, infections, heavy metals, EMF exposure, medications, and excitotoxins
  • Why root-cause evaluation matters when symptoms persist or progress
  • Foundational habits involving sleep, movement, food quality, parsley and apigenin, EMF reduction, and toxin avoidance

episodes.title: Brain Fog, Part 2 - Testing and Basic Solutions

description.full:
When brain fog lasts or comes with memory, focus, word-finding, or speech changes, what should a thoughtful evaluation consider?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M builds on Part 1 with a practical discussion of testing, clinical red flags, and foundational brain-supportive habits.

Topics include:

  • When the duration, frequency, or pattern of brain fog deserves closer evaluation
  • Systemic inflammation and the relationship between body and brain inflammation
  • Full Epstein-Barr virus panels, including VCA IgG and IgM, EBNA, and Early Antigen
  • Mold and mycotoxin testing when exposure history supports it
  • Homocysteine and other blood clues that may inform a workup
  • When progressive cognitive change or neurological red flags may make brain imaging appropriate
  • Sleep, exercise, food quality, EMF reduction, and toxin avoidance while root causes are being investigated

episodes.title: Insomnia - Causes and Practical Sleep Strategies

description.full:
Whether the problem is falling asleep, staying asleep, or getting enough restorative hours, better sleep begins with understanding the pattern.

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains common forms of insomnia and offers practical ways to improve sleep timing, light exposure, wind-down routines, and daytime habits.

Topics include:

  • Sleep-onset insomnia, sleep-maintenance insomnia, and insufficient sleep duration
  • Why consistent bedtimes and complete sleep cycles matter
  • Teenagers, delayed sleep phase, and the role of schedule
  • Blue-light reduction, reading, morning light, and daytime exercise
  • Caffeine timing, chocolate, alcohol, antihistamines, and evening habits
  • Stress tools including a written mind dump and EFT tapping
  • Properly timed melatonin and selected homeopathic products discussed in the episode

episodes.title: Electromagnetic Frequencies (EMF) - Practical Ways to Reduce Exposure

description.full:
Phones, WiFi, Bluetooth, vehicles, appliances, and home wiring create different kinds of electromagnetic exposure. Which sources can you measure, and which practical changes may reduce exposure?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M discusses radio frequency, electromagnetic fields, electrical fields, the blood-brain barrier, sleep, and practical mitigation strategies.

Topics include:

  • Radio frequency from phones, WiFi, Bluetooth, wireless earbuds, and towers
  • Electromagnetic fields from appliances, electric and hybrid vehicles, and plugged-in devices
  • Electrical fields from home wiring
  • Potential relationships among exposure, the blood-brain barrier, headaches, brain fog, sleep, and inflammation
  • Wired peripherals, air-tube headsets, airplane mode, distance, Ethernet, and turning off unused radios
  • Testing vehicles, considering smart-meter options, and measuring home and workplace exposure
  • Safe and Sound II and TriField meters, shielding approaches, and professional assessments

episodes.title: Energy - Understanding Fatigue and Mitochondrial Health

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M takes a functional-medicine look at energy, fatigue, mitochondrial health, and the importance of investigating root causes.

episodes.title: Concussion - What Happens in the Brain

description.full:
A concussion can affect far more than what appears on a routine scan. What actually happens in the brain, and why can symptoms persist even without a direct hit to the head?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains concussion and traumatic brain injury mechanisms and why care should go beyond ruling out a brain bleed and simply waiting.

Topics include:

  • Structural injury, neural shearing, excitotoxicity, and neuroinflammation
  • Oxidative stress, hypoxia, and blood-brain barrier disruption
  • Brain autoimmunity, hormones, pituitary involvement, and vagus nerve dysfunction
  • Mitochondrial dysfunction, protein-folding abnormalities, neurogenesis, and synaptogenesis
  • Gut-microbiome changes after injury
  • Brain fog, headache, dizziness, emotional instability, fatigue, sleepiness, and brain-based fatigue
  • Why a concussion can occur without the head directly striking an object

episodes.title: The Brain on Fire - Neuroinflammation After Concussion

description.full:
After a concussion, symptoms can improve before the brain has rebuilt its full reserve. What does that mean for reinjury risk, neuroinflammation, and recovery?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M explains brain reserve, glial cells, inflammatory and repair-oriented microglia, and research-informed factors he considers after concussion.

Topics include:

  • Why brain reserve can differ across regions and why symptom relief does not always mean full recovery
  • Protecting a healing brain from reinjury
  • Astrocytes and the blood-brain barrier
  • Oligodendrocytes, myelin, and neural support
  • Pro-inflammatory M1 and repair-oriented M2 microglial activity
  • Sleep, luteolin, apigenin, vitamin D, omega-3 fats, curcumin, and Nrf2 signaling as research-informed considerations

episodes.title: Food and the Brain - Eating for Brain Health and Concussion Recovery

description.full:
What should you eat when you want a sharper brain—or when the brain is recovering from a concussion or other neurological stress?

In this episode of Dr. M Experienced, with Dr. David Musnick, Dr. M connects food with brain health, neuroinflammation, blood-sugar stability, mitochondria, the gut-brain connection, and neuronal membranes.

Topics include:

  • Apigenin, parsley, and the balance between inflammatory M1 and repair-oriented M2 microglia
  • A parsley, wild-blueberry, and protein smoothie
  • Choline, omega-3 DHA, plasmalogens, and neuronal membranes
  • Nrf2-supportive broccoli sprouts, green tea, turmeric, and rosemary
  • Quercetin-rich capers, red onions, and apples
  • Protein, lower-mercury fish, vegetable diversity, fiber, and the microbiome
  • Advanced glycation end products, acrylamide, heavy metals, BPA, MSG, aspartame, and sugar
  • Ketogenic diets, intermittent fasting, and when they may not be appropriate

Dr. M explains why he may consider gluten-free, cow-dairy-free, or selective short-term elimination strategies in some concussion and neurological cases. These are not universal and should be individualized with an appropriate clinician.
